INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In the metaphor Time is money, what is the meaning? (1 mark)
   A. Clocks are coins
   B. Time is made of paper
   C. Time is valuable and should not be wasted
   D. Money is a clock

2. Where do oral narratives come from? (1 mark)
   A. From elders and storytellers who pass them on
   B. From nowhere
   C. From machines only
   D. From only one book

3. What is extensive reading? (1 mark)
   A. Copying a book
   B. Reading only the title
   C. Reading one word only
   D. Reading many books widely for pleasure

4. How can you find the meaning of a new word in a reader? (1 mark)
   A. Use the context and check a dictionary
   B. Tear the page
   C. Ignore it always
   D. Ask no one

5. A good ending to an imaginative story usually (1 mark)
   A. has no full stops
   B. repeats the title
   C. starts a new problem always
   D. solves the problem or shows the lesson

6. A saying such as It is raining cats and dogs means (1 mark)
   A. dogs and cats are lost
   B. it is raining very heavily
   C. the weather is cold
   D. animals are falling

7. Which sentence uses when correctly? (1 mark)
   A. We when ran.
   B. When we ran home rained it.
   C. When it rained, we ran home.
   D. Rained we when home.

8. What should you do with the events of a story you tell? (1 mark)
   A. Tell them in the order they happened
   B. Never mention the end
   C. Mix them up
   D. Skip the beginning

9. What is scanning? (1 mark)
   A. Singing
   B. Looking quickly for a specific piece of information
   C. Reading for the main idea only
   D. Writing a story

10. What is a service? (1 mark)
   A. A thing you can hold
   B. A kind of coin
   C. A market
   D. Work done for others

11. What is a compound sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Two simple sentences joined by a conjunction
   B. A list
   C. A sentence with one word
   D. A title

12. Which word shows a choice? (1 mark)
   A. or
   B. and
   C. but
   D. so

13. Which of these is a preposition? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. behind
   C. banana
   D. jump

14. Which is a wild animal? (1 mark)
   A. Zebra
   B. Dog
   C. Cow
   D. Hen

15. What should you do while listening to instructions about where to place objects? (1 mark)
   A. Listen to the whole instruction before acting
   B. Move immediately
   C. Look away
   D. Talk

16. The goat is inside the shed. Which preposition shows this? (1 mark)
   A. behind
   B. in
   C. outside
   D. between

17. Which pair of words rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. hen and goat
   B. cow and shade
   C. day and play
   D. water and food

18. Which is a poem's mood if it is joyful? (1 mark)
   A. Angry
   B. Sad
   C. Happy
   D. Sleepy

19. Which is a good ending for a story? (1 mark)
   A. It solves the problem or shows the lesson
   B. It repeats the title
   C. It begins a new topic
   D. It has no meaning

20. What is the problem in a story? (1 mark)
   A. The page
   B. The ending word
   C. The title
   D. The trouble or challenge the characters face

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how a class can start a reading club. (4 marks)

22. List three steps for skimming. (3 marks)

23. List three steps for explaining a proverb. (3 marks)

24. Write one simile and one metaphor about a teacher. (3 marks)

25. Write two compound sentences about shopping using so and but. (4 marks)

26. Write three sentences describing where things are in your classroom. Use a different preposition in each. (3 marks)

27. Explain the difference between a simile and a metaphor and give an example of each. (4 marks)

28. Complete with a simile: The baby slept like a ______. (2 marks)

29. Find the rhyming words in: Feed the hen at break of day, Give her water, let her play. (2 marks)

30. Give two features of a poem. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Time is valuable and should not be wasted
   The metaphor shows the value of time.

2. A — From elders and storytellers who pass them on
   They are passed on by word of mouth.

3. D — Reading many books widely for pleasure
   Extensive reading means reading a lot for enjoyment.

4. A — Use the context and check a dictionary
   Context clues and a dictionary help.

5. D — solves the problem or shows the lesson
   Endings resolve the story.

6. B — it is raining very heavily
   It is an expression for heavy rain.

7. C — When it rained, we ran home.
   It shows two events joined by time.

8. A — Tell them in the order they happened
   Order helps listeners follow.

9. B — Looking quickly for a specific piece of information
   Scanning searches for a detail.

10. D — Work done for others
   Cutting hair is a service.

11. A — Two simple sentences joined by a conjunction
   It joins two ideas.

12. A — or
   Or offers a choice.

13. B — behind
   Behind shows position.

14. A — Zebra
   Zebras live freely on the plains.

15. A — Listen to the whole instruction before acting
   Full listening avoids mistakes.

16. B — in
   In shows something is inside.

17. C — day and play
   Day and play end in the same sound.

18. C — Happy
   A joyful poem has a happy mood.

19. A — It solves the problem or shows the lesson
   Endings resolve the story.

20. D — The trouble or challenge the characters face
   The problem drives the events.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Collect books, choose a name and a librarian, agree on rules for borrowing, meet regularly to read and share books, and record who borrowed each book.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct points.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read headings, read the first sentence of each paragraph, glance over the rest, say the main idea.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say it slowly, picture what it shows, decide the lesson, think of a real situation, explain in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Simile: The teacher is as patient as a rock. Metaphor: The teacher is a walking dictionary.
   Working / marking points: One mark for a simile, one for a metaphor, one for clearly showing the difference.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: I had money, so I bought bread. I wanted a toy, but it was too costly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence and one for each correct comma.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences, for example The board is in front of the class. My bag is under my desk. The teacher stands beside the door.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: A simile compares using like or as, for example as quick as lightning. A metaphor says one thing is another, for example Time is money.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition and one for each example.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: log (or a stone, or any suitable comparison)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a suitable comparison and one for keeping like.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: day and play
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Short lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, images (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
